Specific Comments
1. Our major concern with the RISP, as planned, is the potential for an uncontrolled release of hydrocarbons to the environment due to sediment drilling operations. Although the draft statement recognizes this hazard, it does not present the information necessary for a thorough environmental evaluation of the risks involved. For example, the statement "to drill to 100m is safe, to 150m is marginal" (page 30) should be explained further. As the sediment drilling operation is scheduled for the 1975-76 austral summer, sufficient time exists to better plan for petroleum release possibilities which may occur during that phase of the project. We need to know what precautions are being taken to minimise the probability for hydrocarbon release and what contingency plans will be followed in the event hydrocarbons are released into the environment.
2. The use of diesel oil as a drilling fluid should be avoided unless adequate means are available to recapture the fluid from both sea and ice environments. The final statement should address this matter in greater detail.
3. Under current plans, sanitary wastes will be discharged untreated into the surface and subsurface levels of the firm. To the best of our knowledge there would be no significant degradation of these wastes in the length of time that it would take these materials to reach the ocean. The final statement should discuss the alternative method of incineration for the disposal of sanitary wastes. If care is taken to keep the sanitary wastes separate from other liquid wastes, incineration may be a preferable method at little additional cost.
